title: Counting inversions: all pairs vs merge sort
problem_statement: Given a sequence a_1..a_n, count the pairs i < j with a_i > a_j.

algorithms.name: all pairs
algorithms.pseudocode: count pairs i < j with a_i > a_j

algorithms.name: merge-sort counting
algorithms.idea: Sort recursively and count cross inversions while merging: a right-half element placed before the remaining left-half elements is inverted with each of them.
algorithms.correctness: Every inversion lies within the left half, within the right half, or across; cross inversions are counted exactly once during the merge (CLRS Problem 2-4).

relationship: Theta(n^2) -> Theta(n log n) by divide and conquer. Faster algorithms exist in the word-RAM model (O(n sqrt(log n)), Chan & Pătraşcu 2010).

sources.authors: Cormen, T. H.; Leiserson, C. E.; Rivest, R. L.; Stein, C.
sources.title: Introduction to Algorithms (3rd ed.)
The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 3: Sorting and Searching (2nd ed.)
Counting Inversions, Offline Orthogonal Range Counting, and Related Problems
sources.note: O(n sqrt(log n)) in the word RAM.

verification.method: V1: both agree with each other and with an independent Fenwick-tree oracle on random sequences with duplicates, n = 0..500. V2: runtimes fitted against n^2 and n log n.

caveats: The V2 fit cannot resolve the log factor; it rules out quadratic behaviour of the merge method.
